events.definition: An event involving the effect of the closure of an aerodrome. Aerodrome: A defined area on land or water (including any buildings, installations and equipment) intended to be used either wholly or in part for the arrival, departure and surface movement of aircraft. events.definition: Stabilized approach: These recommended parameters define a stabilized approach and should be met by 1,000 feet above airport elevation in IMC or 500 feet in VMC: 1. The aircraft is on the correct flight path; 2. Only small changes in heading/pitch are required to maintain the correct flight path; 3. The aircraft speed is not more than VREF + 20 knots indicated airspeed and not less than VREF; 4. The aircraft is in the correct landing configuration; 5. Sink rate is no greater than 1,000 feet per minute; if an approach requires a sink rate greater than 1,000 feet per minute, a special briefing should be conducted; 6. Power setting is appropriate for the aircraft configuration and is not below the minimum power for approach as defined by the aircraft operating manual; 7. All briefings and checklists have been conducted; 8. Specific types of approaches are stabilized if they also fulfill the following: instrument landing system (ILS) approaches must be flown within one dot of the glide slope and localizer; a Category II or Category III ILS approach must be flown within the expanded localizer band; during a circling approach, wings should be level on final when the aircraft reaches 300 feet above airport elevation; and, 9. Unique approach procedures or abnormal conditions requiring a deviation from the above elements of a stabilized approach require a special briefing. events.name: Aircraft encounter with turbulence
events.definition: Encounter with any or all of a) clear air turbulence (CAT) b) turbulence in cloud c) vortex / wake turbulence also to be used in events in which the aircraft was damaged by turbulence. CAT: Clear Air Turbulence (CAT) is the bumpiness experienced by aircraft at high altitudes (above 18,000 feet) in either cloud- free conditions or in stratiform clouds. CAT occurs when undulations (known as gravity waves) in the upper atmosphere become steep and unstable, then break down into chaotic motion. The scale of wave motion that normally affects jet aircraft is on the order of ~10 meters to ~1-2 kilometers. These unstable waves occur when vertical wind shear becomes locally excessive, allowing the waves to overcome the stability of environmental temperature conditions. This condition is known as Kelvin-Helmholtz instability. Most CAT occurs on the fringes of (not within the core of) the jet stream, in the vicinity of upper level frontal zones where temperature contrasts are strong. CAT may also occur when strong winds cross a mountain range in certain thermal conditions, allowing gravity waves to amplify and propagate vertically toward the stratosphere. These 'mountain waves' may be smooth undulations, resulting in updrafts and downdrafts (UDDF in pilot report code), or can break down into smaller scale turbulence. A third instance in which CAT occurs is when strong winds encounter the tops of thunderstorm clouds, resulting in strong shear waves that extend well downstream from the convective cloud.

events.name: Aircraft encountered vortex/wake turbulence
events.definition: Wake turbulence: Turbulent air behind an aircraft caused by any of the following: (a) wing-tip vortices; (b) rotor-tip vortices; (c) jet-engine thrust stream or jet blast; (d) rotor downwash; (e) prop wash. Wing tip vortex: A circular pattern of air current created by the movement of an airfoil through the air when the airfoil is generating lift. As an airfoil moves through the atmosphere in sustained flight, an area of high pressure is created beneath it and an area of low pressure is created above it. The air flowing from the high-pressure area to the low-pressure area around and about the tips of the airfoil tends to roll up into two rapidly rotating vortices, cylindrical in shape. These vortices are the predominant parts of aircraft wake turbulence and their rotational force is dependent upon the wing loading, gross weight, and speed of the generating aircraft. The vortices from medium to heavy aircraft can be of extremely high velocity and hazardous to smaller aircraft.

Includes gear safety switches which prevent inadvertent actuation such as squat or air/ground sensor. Typical parts are relay, switch bracket, lamp, horn, up lock switch, down lock switch and in transit switch.

events.name: Auxiliary landing gear related event (ATA Code:3270)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3270) An event involving the devices such as tail skids on tricycle gear aircraft used to stabilize the aircraft on the ground and to prevent ground contact damage. This code is also used for supplementary wheels on rotorcraft, skids for ground handling but not for skids or amphibian/seaplane floats, hull or associated retractable landing gear. Does not include auxiliary or emergency landing gear extension systems.

events.name: Other gear collapsed/retracted
events.definition: An event involving the collapse or retraction of gear other than the nose, tail or main gear, while it is supporting the weight of the aircraft.

events.name: Aircraft lighting related event (ATA Code:3300)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3300) An event involving the units and components which provide for external and internal illumination. Includes light fixtures, switches and wiring. Does not include warning lights for individual systems.

events.name: Navigation systems related event (ATA Code:3400)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3400) An event involving the units and components which provide aircraft navigational information.

events.name: 3410 Flight Environment Data systems realeted event
events.definition: Events related to that portion of the system which senses environmental conditions and uses the data to influence navigation. Includes such items as Central Air Data Computers, pitot/static systems, air temperature, rate-of-climb, airspeed, high speed warning, altitude, altitude reporting, altimeter correction system, air disturbance detection system, etc.

events.name: Airspeed/Mach indicating system related event (ATA Code:3414)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3414) An event involving the instrument which measures and indicates speed of the aircraft.

events.name: Altitude system related event (ATA Code:3416)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3416) An event involving the altimeters and barometric encoders used to measure and indicate altitude. Also includes the unit which senses and alerts to a change in a pre-selected altitude. Does not include the ground proximity systems. Typical parts are dial, case, pointer and spring.

events.name: Flight management system related event (ATA Code:3418)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3418) An event involving the system which combines navigational data to compute or manage the aircraft's geographical position or theoretical flight path. Typical parts are course computers, flight management computers, performance data computers, associated control display units and warning annunciators.

events.name: 3420 Attitude and direction data system related event (ATA Code:3420)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3420) An event involving the system components and parts which use magnetic, gyroscopic, and inertia forces to indicate an aircraft attitude and direction. Includes such items as the inertial reference system (IRS).

events.name: Landing and taxi aids related event (ATA Code:3430)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3430) An event involving the system providing guidance during approach, landing and taxiing. Includes such items as, ILS, paravisual director, ground guidance systems and markers.

events.name: Independent position determining system related event (ATA Code:3440)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3440) An event involving the system which provides information to determine the aircraft's position and is primarily independent of ground installations. Typical parts are star tracker and sextants/octants.

events.name: Ground proximity warning system related event (ATA Code:3444)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3444) An event involving the system which detects and alerts flight crew to potential terrain hazards. Includes the antenna which transmits and receives an electronic signal for the radio altimeter equipment used for terrain-to-aircraft distance. Also includes the component which interprets a radio signal reflected back to a receiver to determine distance from the nearest terrain; and the component which process the warning computer input signals from various sources in order to determine if and when the crew should be alerted of a terrain hazard.

events.name: Ground proximity warning system nuisance alarm
events.definition: An event involving nuisance warnings by the aircraft's ground proximity warning system.

events.name: Other ground proximity warning system related event
events.definition: An event involving the aircraft's ground proximity warning system other than a nuisance warning.

events.name: Airborne collision avoidance system/traffic alert and collision avoidance system related
events.short: Airborne collision avoidance system/traffic alert and collision avoidance system related
path: Airborne collision avoidance system/traffic alert and collision avoidance system related
events.definition: event (ATA Code:3445) (3445 ACAS/TCAS) (ATA Code:3445) An event involving the system which provides information to determine aircraft position and is primarily independent of ground installations (i.e., traffic alert and collision avoidance system TCAS). Typical parts are collision avoidance monitoring units.

events.name: ACAS/TCAS nuisance alarm
path: Airborne collision avoidance system/traffic alert and collision avoidance system related
events.definition: An event involving a nuisance alarm from the aircraft's airborne collision avoidance system or traffic alert and collision avoidance system.

events.name: 3450 Dependent Position Determining System related event
events.definition: Events related to that portion of the system which provides information to determine position and is mainly dependent on ground installations or orbital satellites. Includes items such as DME, transponders, radio compass, LORAN, VOR, ADF, OMEGA, GLOBAL POSITIONING, etc.

events.name: Flight management system related event (ATA Code:3460)
events.definition: An event involving the system which combines navigational data to compute or manage the aircraft's geographical position or theoretical flight path. Typical parts are course computers, flight management computers, performance data computers, associated control display units and warning annunciators.

events.name: Oxygen system related event (ATA Code:3500)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3500) An event involving the units and components which store, regulate and deliver breathing oxygen to the passengers and crew. Typical parts are bottles, relief valves, shut-off valves, outlets, regulators, masks and walk-around bottles.

events.name: Pneumatic system related event (ATA Code:3600)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3600) An event involving the units and components which deliver large volumes of compressed air from a power source to connecting points for other systems such as air conditioning, pressurization and de-icing.

events.name: Vacuum system related event (ATA Code:3700)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3700) An event involving the units and components used to generate, deliver and regulate negative air pressure.

events.name: Drinkable/waste water system related event (ATA Code:3800)
events.definition: (ATA Code:3800) An event involving the fixed units and components which store and deliver fresh water. Also includes those fixed components which store and furnish a means of removal of water and waste.

events.name: 4100 Water ballast system
events.definition: Event related to units and components provided for the storage, balancing, control, filling, discharge, and dumping of water ballast.

events.name: 4200 Integrated modular avionics related event
events.definition: Event related to computing devices that can host software applications for system functions that had traditionally been implemented in dedicated hardware. The actual system functions are covered in their respective ATA chapters.

events.name: 4400 Cabin systems related event
events.definition: Event related to units and components which furnish a means of entertaining the passengers and providing communication within the aircraft and between the aircraft cabin and ground stations. Includes voice, data, music and video transmissions. Does not include SATCOM, HF, VHF, UHF and all transmitting/receiving equipment, antennas, etc., which are covered in Chapter 23 or Chapter 46.

events.name: 4500 Central Maintenance Computer
events.definition: Event related to units, components and associated system which interfaces with multiple aircraft systems. Contains checkout and fault isolation procedures using a central computer complex and/or standard fault isolation procedures to locate a single system or component malfunction.

events.name: 4600 Information systems
events.definition: Event related to units and components which furnish a means of storing, updating, and retrieving digital information traditionally provided on paper, microfilm, or microfiche. Includes units that are dedicated to the information storage and retrieval function such as the Electronic Library mass storage and controller. Does not include units or components installed for other uses and shared with other systems, such as flight deck printer or general use display.

events.name: 4700 Inert gas system related event
events.definition: Event relted to units and components used to generate, store, deliver and regulate inert gas. Includes regulators, lines, manifolds, etc.

events.name: Auxiliary power unit related event (ATA Code:4900)
events.definition: (ATA Code:4900) An event involving the airborne auxiliary power units (APU) installed on aircraft for the purpose of generating and supplying a single type or combination of auxiliary electric, hydraulic, pneumatic or other power. Does not include generators, alternators, hydraulic pumps or their connecting systems which supply and deliver power to their respective aircraft systems.

events.name: 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments related events
events.definition: Those compartments for storage of cargo and various components and accessories. Includes those systems used to load/unload cargo and other cargo related systems. Does not include aircraft structure which is in Capter 53

events.name: 5010 Cargo Compartments related events
events.definition: Event related to compartments for the storage of cargo

events.name: Cargo related event
events.definition: An event involving the aircraft's cargo.

events.name: Cargo leak
events.definition: An event involving a leak from the aircraft's cargo other than a radiation leak.

events.name: Cargo shifted
events.definition: An event involving a shift of the aircraft's cargo after the aircraft was loaded.

events.name: Cargo smoke/fumes/fire
events.definition: An event involving smoke, fumes or fire in the aircraft's cargo compartment.

events.name: Cargo radiation leak
events.definition: An event involving a leak of radioactive material, or radiation, from the aircraft's cargo.

events.name: Cargo/sling load dropped
events.definition: Cargo/sling load dropped: to used when the dropping of the load was the rwsult of any failure. Intentional dropping of the sling load is covered under 'consequential events'

events.name: 5020 Cargo Loading Systems related event
events.definition: Events related to systems which have components which are or can be mounted on the aircraft and used to load/unload, restrain, guide or service cargo. Includes drive systems, rollers, latches, restraint nets etc.

events.name: 5030 Cargo Related Systems related events
events.definition: Events related to systems which are related to loading/unloading of cargo. Includes aircraft levelling, loader alignment systems etc. Does not include Cargo Loading Systems.

events.name: 5050 Accessory Compartments related event
events.definition: Event related to compartments used for the housing of various components and accessories. Includes wheel wells, tail- hydraulic-electrical/electronic equipment racks, main battery structure etc.

events.name: 5060 Insulation
events.definition: Events related to insulation blankets which are used for heat and sound insulation. Includes cargo compartments and accessory compartments, insulation, etc.

events.name: Standard practices and structures (ATA Code:5100)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5100) An event involving the standard practices and general procedures for typical repairs applicable to the aircraft's airframe or structure.

events.name: Airframe structure - general related event (ATA Code:5101)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5101) An event involving aircraft structural problems of a general nature which affects two or more areas. Includes reports of lightning strikes which cannot be associated with a specific code.

events.name: Aircraft's doors related event (ATA Code:5200)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5200) An event involving any of the removable units used for entrance or exit and for enclosing other structure contained within the fuselage. Includes passenger and crew doors, cargo doors and emergency exits. Electrical and hydraulic systems associated with door control are included as appropriate.

events.name: Doors - general related event (ATA Code:5201)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5201) An event involving any of the aircraft's doors in general.

events.name: Door opening
events.definition: An event involving the inadvertent or intentional opening of any of the aircraft's doors.

events.name: Door separation
events.definition: An event involving the separation of any of the aircraft's doors.

events.name: Door warning system related event
events.definition: An event involving the aircraft's door warning system.

events.name: Aircraft's fuselage structure related event (ATA Code:5300)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5300) An event involving the structural units and associated components and members which make up the compartments for crew, passengers, equipment, cargo and the structure of the envelope and gondola of airships.

events.name: Airframe failure - other than general breakup (ATA Code:5301)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5301) An event involving a failure of the aircraft's airframe or structure other than a general disintegration or break-up.

events.name: Airframe general disintegration or break-up (ATA Code:5302)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5302) An event involving a general disintegration or break-up of the aircraft's airframe or structure.

events.name: Aircraft engine nacelle or pylon structure related event (ATA Code:5400)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5400) An event involving the structural units and associated components and members which furnish a means of mounting and housing the power plant or rotor assembly. Includes the structure of power plant cowling inclusive of the structural portion of the inlet whether or not integral with the aircraft. Structural portions of the exhaust system are excluded where they are not integral with the airframe.

events.name: Aircraft empennage stucture related event (ATA Code:5500)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5500) An event involving the horizontal and vertical stabilizers including the structure of the elevator and rudder. This code is also used for reports that pertain to flying wires.

events.name: 5510 Horizontal Stabilizer/Canard Structure related event
events.definition: Event related to the horizontal airfoil of the tail or nose section to which the elevator is attached. Includes items such as spars, ribs, stringers, skins, access covers, tips, attach/attached fittings, etc.

events.name: Aircraft elevator related event (ATA Code:5520)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5520) An event involving the structural aspects of the movable aerofoil hinged to the horizontal stabilizer for longitudinal control. Includes the 'ruddervator' on V-tail aircraft and balance weights. Does not include the stabilator structure.

events.name: 5530 Vertical Stabilizer related event
events.definition: Event related to the vertical airfoil to which the rudder is attached. Includes items such as spars, ribs, stringers, skins, access covers, tips, attach/attached fittings, etc.

events.name: Aircraft rudder related event (ATA Code:5540)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5540) An event involving the structural aspects of the vertical aerofoil hinged to the vertical stabilizer. Does not include the actuators, actuator mechanism or mounting. Typical parts are hinge, hinge fittings, bearing, bolt and miscellaneous structure.

events.name: Aircraft windows/windshields related event (ATA Code:5600)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5600) An event involving the fuselage and crew compartment windows inclusive of windshields.

events.name: Aircraft's windows in general related event (ATA Code:5601)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5601) An event involving the aircraft's windows in general.

events.name: Window separation in flight
events.definition: An event involving the separation in flight of an aircraft window.

events.name: 5610 Flight compartment window
events.definition: 5610 Flight compartment window: includes cockpit windows, cockpit overhead canopies, observation windows, and windshield panels in the flight compartment. Includes attachment and sliding feature of sliding windows. For cockpit windows including the breakage of electrically heated windshield panels regardless of cause.

events.name: Aircraft wing structure related event (ATA Code:5700)
events.definition: (ATA Code:5700) An event involving the centre wing and outer wing structural units and associated components and members which support the aircraft in flight. This code should be used for general reports of the primary wing structure. Control surfaces (on the wing) related event (ATA Code:5750) (5750 Control surfaces)                                    1575000   * (ATA Code:5750) An event involving the control surfaces which are attached to the wing.

events.name: 5740 Wing Leading Edge and Leading Edge Devices
events.short: 5740 Wing Leading Edge and Leading Edge Devices
path: 5740 Wing Leading Edge and Leading Edge Devices
events.definition: Event related to skins and structure of the wing leading edge and removable leading edge airfoils such as flaps, slats, attach/attached fittings, etc.

events.name: 5750 Wing Trailing Edge / Trailing Edge Devices
events.short: 5750 Wing Trailing Edge / Trailing Edge Devices
path: 5750 Wing Trailing Edge / Trailing Edge Devices
events.definition: Event related to skins and structure of the wing and trailing edge and removable edge airfoils such as flaps and attach/attached fittings

events.name: 6000 STANDARD PRACTICES - PROPELLER/ROTOR
events.definition: (ATA Code 6000) STANDARD PRACTICES - PROPELLER/ROTOR

events.name: Propellers related event (ATA Code:6100)
events.definition: (ATA Code:6100) An event involving the complete mechanical or electrical propeller, governor, alternators, pumps, motors those units and components external to or integral with the engine used to control the propeller blade angle. Includes the propulsor duct assemblies, aerodynamic fairing of mechanical components, stators and vectoring systems.

events.name: Aircraft's propellers related event (ATA Code:6101)
events.definition: (ATA Code:6101) An event involving any of the aircraft's propellers in general.

events.name: Propeller over-speed
events.definition: An event involving a propeller over-speed.

events.name: Propeller separation
events.definition: An event involving the separation of a propeller from its engine.

events.name: Propeller control
events.definition: An event related to the control of a propeller.

events.name: Rotorcraft main rotor systems related event (ATA Code:6200)
events.definition: (ATA Code:6200) An event involving the rotorcraft main rotor systems. Main rotor: the rotor that supplies the principal lift to a rotorcraft.

events.name: Helicopter's main rotor in general related event (ATA Code:6201)
events.definition: (ATA Code:6201) An event involving a helicopter's main rotor in general. Main rotor: the rotor that supplies the principal lift to a rotorcraft.

events.name: Main rotor blade flapping
events.definition: An event involving flapping of the helicopter's main rotor blades.

events.name: Main rotor drive system related event (ATA Code:6300)
events.definition: (ATA Code:6300) An event involving the main rotor drive system.

events.name: Main rotor drive shaft (ATA Code:6301)
events.definition: (ATA Code:6301) An event involving the helicopter's main rotor drive shaft.

events.name: Main rotor transmission/gearbox (ATA Code:6320)
events.definition: (ATA Code:6320) An event involving the component which transmits engine power to rotary motion in the main rotor mast. Includes mechanical power take-off and accessory drives but does not include the accessories such as hydraulic pumps and alternators. Includes gearbox lubricating system. Typical parts are gearbox, case, shaft, gear, pump, seal and sun gear.

events.name: Gearbox chip warning
events.definition: Gearbox chip warning

events.name: Rotorcraft tail rotor system related event (ATA Code:6400)
events.definition: (ATA Code:6400) An event involving the rotorcraft tail rotor system.

events.name: Tail rotor drive system related event (ATA Code:6500)
events.definition: (ATA Code:6500) An event involving the rotorcraft's tail rotor drive system.

events.name: Tail rotor drive shaft related event (ATA Code:6510)
events.definition: (ATA Code:6510) An event involving the shafts, flexible couplings and bearings, from the main rotor transmission to the tail rotor assembly. Typical parts shaft, coupling, bearing and hanger.

events.name: Tail rotor gearbox (90 deg) related event (ATA Code:6520) (6520 Tail rotor gearbox (90 deg))
events.short: Tail rotor gearbox (90 deg) related event (ATA Code:6520) (6520 Tail rotor gearbox (90 deg))
path: Tail rotor gearbox (90 deg) related event (ATA Code:6520) (6520 Tail rotor gearbox (90 deg))
events.definition: (ATA Code:6520) An event involving the helicopter's tail rotor 90 degree gearbox.

events.name: Tail rotor gearbox (45 deg) related event (ATA Code:6530) (6530 Tail rotor gearbox (45 deg))
events.short: Tail rotor gearbox (45 deg) related event (ATA Code:6530) (6530 Tail rotor gearbox (45 deg))
path: Tail rotor gearbox (45 deg) related event (ATA Code:6530) (6530 Tail rotor gearbox (45 deg))
events.definition: (ATA Code:6530) An event involving the helicopter's tail rotor 45 degree gearbox.

events.name: 6600 Folding blades/pylon
events.definition: Event related to the whole of the system ensuring automatic or manual folding and spreading of the rotor blades and/or tail pylon.

events.name: Rotorcraft flight control systems related event (ATA Code:6700)
events.definition: (ATA Code:6700) An event involving the rotorcraft control systems.

events.name: 7000 STANDARD PRACTICES - ENGINES
events.definition: (ATA Code 7000) STANDARD PRACTICES - ENGINES

events.name: Powerplant package related event (ATA Code:7100)
events.definition: (ATA Code:7100) An event involving the power plant package.

events.name: Turbine engine related event (ATA Code:7200)
events.definition: (ATA Code:7200) An event involving the units and components which are used to induce and convert fuel-air mixture into power, and transmit power to the propeller shaft (if any) and accessory drives. Includes reports pertaining to bird strikes to engines/cowling.

events.name: Turbine engine generally (ATA Code:7201)
events.definition: (ATA Code:7201) An event involving a turbine engine generally.

events.name: Turbine engine - tearaway
events.definition: An event involving a turbine engine tearaway.

events.name: Turbine engine - uncontained failure
events.definition: An event involving the failure of a turbine engine's containment system, an engine failure in which parts of the engine exited the nacelle.

events.name: Turbine engine - mechanical failure
events.definition: An event involving a mechanical failure of a turbine engine, i.e. something broke etc.

events.name: Turbine engine - non mechanical failure
events.definition: An event involving a non-mechanical failure of a turbine engine, the engine failed even though the mechanics of the engine were intact.

events.name: Simulated failure of a turbine engine
events.definition: An event involving a simulated failure of a turbine engine.

events.name: Turbine Engine fuel starvation
events.definition: An event involving a loss of power from a turbine engine due to fuel starvation. Fuel Starvation: Deprivation or insufficient supply of fuel to the engine.

events.name: Turbine Engine asymmetric thrust
events.definition: An event involving asymmetric thrust due to a loss of power from a turbine engine.

events.name: Turbine engine multiple failures
events.definition: An event involving multiple failures of the aircraft's turbine engines.

events.name: Turbine engine gearbox related event
events.definition: An event involving a failure of a gearbox in one of the aircraft's turbine engines

events.name: Turbine engine - vibration
events.definition: Turbine engine - vibration

events.name: Turbine engine chip warning
events.definition: Turbine engine chip warning

events.name: Engine fuel system and control related event (ATA Code:7300)
events.definition: (ATA Code:7300) An event involving turbine or reciprocating engine fuel and control systems of the engine.

events.name: Engine ignition system related event (ATA Code:7400)
events.definition: (ATA Code:7400) An event involving the aircraft's engine ignition system.

events.name: Engine air system related event (ATA Code:7500)
events.definition: (ATA Code:7500) An event involving the turbine engine compressor bleed air systems used to control the flow of air through the engine, cooling air systems, and heated air for engine anti-icing.

events.name: Engine controls related event (ATA Code:7600)
events.definition: (ATA Code:7600) An event involving the controls which govern the operation of the engine. Includes units and components which are interconnected for emergency shutdown. For turboprop engines, includes linkages and controls to the co-ordinator or equivalent to the propeller governor, fuel control unit or other units being controlled. For reciprocating engines, includes controls for blowers.

events.name: Engine indicating system related event (ATA Code:7700)
events.definition: (ATA Code:7700) An event involving engine indicating system discrepancies.

events.name: Engine exhaust system related event (ATA Code:7800)
events.definition: (ATA Code:7800) An event involving engine exhaust system defects.

events.name: Thrust reverser system related event (ATA Code:7830)
events.definition: (ATA Code:7830) An event involving the airframe furnished system and components mounted at turbo-jet engine exhaust tailpipes to direct engine thrust forward for deceleration. Does not include the engine tailpipe. Typical parts are door, flex drive, relay, solenoid, switch, switch arm, bolt, valve, line, deploy line, rail, cable, actuator, actuator rod, connector plug, seal, support, fitting, shaft, link, nozzle and hose.

events.name: Engine oil system related event (ATA Code:7900)
events.definition: (ATA Code:7900) An event involving the system units external to the engine which store and deliver engine lubricating oil to and from either turbine or reciprocating engines.

events.name: Engine starting system related event (ATA Code:8000)
events.definition: (ATA Code:8000) An event involving the units, components and associated systems used for starting the engine. Includes electrical, inertia air or other starter systems.

events.name: Exhaust turbine system (reciprocating engine only) related event (ATA Code:8100)
events.definition: (ATA Code:8100) An event involving the exhaust turbine systems for reciprocating engines. Includes power recovery turbine assemblies and turbo-supercharger units when external to the engine.

events.name: Engine water injection system related event (ATA Code:8200)
events.definition: (ATA Code:8200) An event involving the system components and parts which inject a water mixture into induction system of turbine and reciprocating engines. Typical parts are pump, switch, tank and valve.

events.name: Powerplant accessory gearbox related event (ATA Code:8300)
events.definition: (ATA Code:8300) An event involving the units and components which are remotely installed and connected to the engine by a drive shaft but does not include those accessory drives which are bolted to and are immediately adjacent to the engine.

events.name: 8400 PROPULSION AUGMENTATION
events.definition: (ATA Code 8400) Those units and components that, independent of the primary propulsion system, furnish additional thrust of short duration. Includes solid or liquid propellants, controls, indicators, etc.

events.name: Reciprocating engine related event (ATA Code:8500)
events.definition: (ATA Code:8500) An event involving reciprocating engine problems, e.g. over temperature, metal contamination and vibration.

events.name: Reciprocating engine in general (ATA Code:8501)
events.definition: (ATA Code:8501) An event involving a reciprocating engine in general.

events.name: Reciprocating engine tearaway
events.definition: An event involving a reciprocating engine tearaway, i.e. the engine separated from the aircraft.

events.name: Reciprocating engine - uncontained failure
events.definition: An event involving an uncontained failure in a reciprocating engine.

events.name: Reciprocating engine - mechanical failure
events.definition: An event involving a mechanical failure in a reciprocating engine

events.name: Power loss in a reciprocating engine due to non-mechanical failure
events.definition: An event involving a power loss in a reciprocating engine due to non-mechanical failure.

events.name: Reciprocating engine - simulated failure
events.definition: An event involving a simulated power loss in a reciprocating engine.

events.name: Reciprocating engine - fuel starvation
events.definition: An event involving a power loss in a reciprocating engine due to fuel starvation.

events.name: Reciprocating engine - carburetor icing
events.definition: An event involving a power loss in a reciprocating engine due to carburetor icing.

events.name: Failure of more than one reciprocating engine
events.definition: An event involving multiple failures of the aircraft's reciprocating engines.

events.name: Reciprocating engine - gearbox failure
events.definition: An event involving a failure of a reciprocating engine gearbox.

events.name: Reciprocating engine - vibration
events.definition: Reciprocating engine - Vibration

events.name: 9100 CHARTS
events.definition: (ATA Code 9100) Miscellaneous charts not applicable to any particular system, such as spare wire charts, junction box charts, disconnect plug charts, conduit and wire routing charts, rigid tube charts, flexible hose charts and control cab

events.name: Non-component specific events
events.definition: Non-component specific events: Events not related to a specific component or which may involve several systems at the same time, e.g. fires.

events.name: Decompression
events.definition: Decompression events that do not include explosive decompression which has its own event type.

events.name: Explosions / fire/ fumes / smoke
events.definition: Events involving explosions / fire/ fumes / smoke

events.name: Explosion
events.definition: Explosion - to be used when the location of the explosion was not provided or could not be established.

events.name: Explosion - Cockpit
events.definition: Explosion - Cockpit: an explosion in the cockpit.

events.name: Explosion - Passenger cabin
events.definition: Explosion - Passenger cabin

events.name: Explosion - Cargo hold / cargo pod
events.definition: Explosion - Cargo hold / cargo pod

events.name: Explosion - Galley
events.definition: Explosion - Galley

events.name: Explosion - Lavatory
events.definition: Explosion - Lavatory

events.name: Explosion - Avionics bay
events.definition: Explosion - Avionics bay

events.name: Explosion - Powerplant
events.definition: Explosion - Powerplant: if the explosion leads to a loss of power from the powerplant concerned, enter the loss of power as subsequent event.

events.name: Explosion - APU
events.definition: Explosion - APU, includes explosion of the APU as well as explosions in the APU bay.

events.name: Explosion - Other location
events.definition: Explosion - Other location: explosion in a location other than the specific ones mentioned in the list. If the location of the explosion is not known, enter 'explosion' as event type only.

events.name: Fire
events.definition: Fire - to be used when the location of the fire was not provided or could not be established.

events.name: Fire - APU

events.definition: Fire - Avionics bay

events.definition: Fire - Cargo hold / pod

events.definition: Fire - Cockpit

events.definition: Fire - crew rest compartment

events.definition: Fire - Galley

events.name: Fire - Landing gear
events.definition: Fire - Landing gear: e.g. by fluids coming into contact with hot brakes.

events.definition: Fire - Lavatory

events.definition: Fire - oven

events.definition: Fire - Passenger cabin

events.definition: Fire - Powerplant. If the fire in the powerplant causes a loss of power, enter the loss of power as subsequent event

events.name: Fire - Tailpipe Fire
events.definition: Fire - Tailpipe Fire in systems other than the main powerplant systems.

events.name: Fire - Other location
events.definition: Fire - Other location: a fire in a location of the aircraft not found on the detailed list.

events.definition: Fumes - to be used when the location of the fumes was not provided or could not be established.

events.name: Fumes - APU
events.definition: Fumes - APU

events.definition: An event involving the civil aviation authority (or administration).

events.name: Consequential events
events.definition: An event evolving from another event.

events.name: Abrupt stop
events.definition: Abrupt stop, e.g. to avoid a collsion with another aircraft / vehicle.

events.name: Active flow control initiated
events.definition: The initiation of flow control occurs when flow restrictions were intended and submitted for enforcement.

events.name: Active flow control performed
events.definition: The performance of flow control occurs when the flow restrictions were imposed and flow control regulation took place.

events.name: Aircraft abandoned / crew ejected or bailed out
events.definition: The aircraft was abandoned, the crew ejected or bailed out.

events.name: Aircraft return
events.definition: The aircraft returned to its point of departure

events.name: Bounced landing
events.definition: Bounced landing: landing involving repeated touch-downs.

events.name: An approach below minima
events.definition: An approach below minima was carried out as the consequence of previous events.

events.name: Cargo dumped
events.definition: Cargo dumped: e.g. dumping the cargo of an agricultural aircraft as a consequence of a preceding event.

events.name: Change aircraft
events.definition: A change of aircraft as the consequence of previous events.

events.name: Clearance cancelled
events.definition: A clearance was cancelled, e.g. as the consequence of a runway incursion.

events.name: Declared emergency
events.definition: A declared emergency as the consequence of previous events.

events.name: Declared emergency - Distress (Mayday)
events.definition: Declared emergency (ICAO Doc 4444) Distress - MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY

events.name: Declared emergency - Urgency (PAN call)
events.definition: Declared emergency (ICAO Doc 4444) Urgency - PAN PAN PAN

events.name: Ditching - forced landing on water
events.definition: A ditching, an unavoidable controlled emergency landing on water as the consequence of previous events.

events.name: Diversion of an aircraft from the intended destination
events.definition: Diversion: the diversion from the intended destination to another one. Note: Diverting to the aerodrome of departure is to be coded 'aircraft returned'.

events.name: Diversion due to operational decision
events.definition: An event involving a diversion by an aircraft due to an operational decision.

events.name: Diversion due to technical reasons
events.definition: An event involving a diversion by an aircraft due to technical reasons.

events.name: Diversion due to weather conditions
events.definition: An event involving a diversion by an aircraft due to weather conditions.

events.name: diversion - due to other reasons
events.definition: An event involving a diversion by an aircraft due to reasons other than those listed above.

events.name: Emergency autorotation (helicopter) (Emergency autorotation (helicopter))
events.definition: An emergency autorotation (helicopter) as the consequence of previous events.

events.name: Emergency cancelled
events.definition: An emergency cancelled as the consequence of previous events.

events.name: Emergency descent
events.definition: An emergency descent as the consequence of previous events. The events mark the decision to carry out the emergency descent. 'Emergency descent' as a sub phase indicates the phase of flight of the aircraft while implementing such a decision.

events.name: Engine shutdown/flameout
events.definition: An Engine shutdown/flameout as the consequence of previous events.

events.name: Engine shutdown - precautionary (soft) (Engine shutdown - precautionary (soft))
events.definition: An Engine shutdown (soft) as the consequence of previous events.

events.name: Engine shutdown (hard) (Engine shutdown (hard))
events.definition: An Engine shutdown (hard) as the consequence of previous events.

events.name: Evacuation
events.definition: Evacuation: Evacuation means the leaving of the aircraft through approved exits and using approved means following the aircraft emergency evacuation procedure. Escape from the wreckage through breaks in the fuselage is not what is meant by 'evacuation'. Unauthorized leaving the aircraft resulting from panic of passengers is also included here.

events.name: Evasive manoeuvre
events.definition: Evasive manoeuvre: a manoeuvre carried out be the crew in order to avoid an aircraft / vehicle / obstacle as the consequence of having it observed or being warned of its presence.

events.name: External load dropped/jettisoned (intentional)
events.definition: The intentional dropping of an external load of a fixed wing aircraft triggered by a preceding event. For helicopters, see events related to helicopter - external load.

events.name: The landing was executed without flaps/slats
events.definition: The landing was executed without flaps/slats being used. This usually results in higher speeds.

events.name: Flight cancellation
events.definition: A flight cancellation as the consequence of previous events.

events.name: Flight delay
events.definition: The flight was delayed as the consequence of a preceding event.

events.name: Fly-past inspection
events.definition: Fly-past inspection: the aircraft is flying over an observation point (e.g. tower) to permit ground staff to inspect the aircraft. Often used to determine whether the landing gear has been properly extended.

events.name: Forced landing
events.definition: Forced landing. Unavoidable landing. A forced landing as the consequence of previous events. Note: forced landing is to be used when the aircraft is landed on land. Use 'Ditching' for forced landings on water.

events.name: Fuel burn off
events.definition: Intentional holding to consume fuel before landing. Usually done in order to prevent overweight landing or to reduce fire hazards.

events.name: Fuel dumping
events.definition: Fuel dumping

events.name: Gravity Gear Extension
events.definition: Gravity Gear Extension

events.name: Handling check
events.definition: Handling check: a check by the crew to determine whether there is any abnormality in handling the aircraft, e.g. after an unusual noise has been heard.

events.name: Missed approach
events.definition: A missed approach as the consequence of previous events. A missed approach is a segment of an instrument approach procedure that is accomplished if the pilot is unable to successfully complete the approach procedure. A successful approach is accomplished when the pilot can get the airport/runway in sight, but not necessarily to a landing.

events.name: Aircraft nosed down/overturned
events.definition: An event involving an aircraft which nosed down or overturned.

events.name: Overweight landing
events.definition: Overweight landing - a landing in which the maximum permissible landing weight was exceeded.

events.name: Precautionary descent
events.definition: A precautionary descent as the consequence of previous events.

events.name: Precautionary landing
events.definition: A precautionary landing as the consequence of previous events. A landing necessitated by apparent impending failure of engines, systems, or components which makes continued flight inadvisable.

events.name: Rejected landing
events.definition: A rejected landing as the consequence of previous events. A rejected landing is an event that occurs when the pilot has the runway in sight and is in a position to land, but is unable to complete the landing. Reasons for rejected landing can be something on the runway, high winds/microburst, mechanical issue (the landing gear does not come down), etc.

events.name: Rejected take-off
events.definition: A rejected take-off as the consequence of previous events.

events.name: High speed rejected take-off (at and above V1)
events.definition: High speed rejected take-off - a take-off rejected at a speed at or above V1.

events.name: Low speed rejected take-off (below V1)
events.definition: A take-off rejected at a speed below V1.

events.name: Rotation - delayed
events.definition: Delayed rotation, e.g. in order to avoid another aircraft

events.name: Rotation - early
events.definition: Rotation - early, e.g. to avoid another vehicle/aircraft in a runway incursion
